name: CCT (Correlated Color Temperature) Preference
description: How correlated color temperature modulates CVA constraints and valuations. Warm CCT (2700-3000K) reduces ProcessingCost and enhances RestorationValue; cool CCT (5000-6500K) increases InterestValue and ControlEfficacy. Neurotype-dependent: PTSD subjects show stronger warm-CCT preference due to safety associations.
theoretical_basis: Knez (1995) on CCT effects on mood and cognition
Deguchi & Sato (1992) on subjective impressions of illumination
Veitch & Newsham (2000) on lighting quality and occupant satisfaction

neurotype_interactions.ptsd: Strong warm-CCT preference; cool CCT increases PredictionError
neurotype_interactions.older_adult: Higher CCT needed for contrast; warm preferred for comfort
neurotype_interactions.depression: Cool CCT beneficial for circadian regulation

basis: Correlated color temperature (CCT) preference varies with time of day, activity, and circadian phase
derivation: Links melanopic sensitivity curves with thermal comfort preferences and color-emotion associations
